questions.question: Combination vehicles:

options.text: Usually have taller trailers than single commercial vehicles.
Usually weigh less than single commercial vehicles.
Need more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more skill to drive. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over than single commercial vehicles.

questions.question: The emergency air line supplies air to the:

options.text: Relay valves.
Trailer air tanks.
Signal line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Trailer air tanks.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) does two things. It supplies air to the trailer air tanks and controls the emergency brakes on combination vehicles.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if a serious leak happens
A valve that stops the trailer from being accidentally released
A valve that keeps the vehicle from going too fast

questions.correctAnswerText: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if a serious leak happens
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a serious leak. The valve closes automatically if pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: Combination vehicles are usually:

options.text: Easier to drive than single commercial vehicles.
Lighter than single commercial vehicles.
Harder to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more skill to drive. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over than single commercial vehicles.

questions.question: The best way to know your trailer has started to skid is by:

options.text: Watching other drivers' faces.
Seeing it in your mirrors.
Feeling it.
Listening to the radio.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seeing it in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: The best way to notice a trailer skid early is to see the trailer move sideways in your mirrors.

questions.question: To prevent a trailer from rolling over, you should:

options.text: Speed up when nearing a corner.
Make sudden steering changes.
Drive faster than the speed limit on ramps.
Drive slowly around corners.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly around corners.
questions.explanation: To lower the risk of a rollover, keep the cargo weight as low as possible and drive slowly around turns.

questions.question: When driving a trailer with ABS, you should:

options.text: Press the brakes less hard than you would in a vehicle without ABS.
Use extra braking force to make the ABS start working.
Brake the same way as you would in a vehicle without ABS.
Avoid braking as often as you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way as you would in a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: When driving a tractor-trailer with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: After coupling, there should be ____ between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

options.text: No space
Very little space
A lot of space
Three inches of space

questions.correctAnswerText: No space
questions.explanation: Before driving, check all couplings. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.question: During a trip, landing gear should be:

options.text: Completely raised.
Completely lowered.
Just barely above the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Completely raised.
questions.explanation: Always completely raise landing gear (trailer supports) before driving. If not raised fully, it could catch on railroad tracks or other hazards on the road.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve should be used:

options.text: To test the trailer brakes.
To check if the trailer and tractor are connected.
To speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: To test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while driving can cause a skid.

questions.question: What do shut-off valves do?

options.text: Stop air from leaving air brake systems.
Stop air from entering air brake systems.
Control vehicles that are out of control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop air from leaving air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. The rear shut-off valve must stay closed to keep air in the braking system.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rollovers?

options.text: Speed up quickly after stopping.
Drive slowly around turns.
Keep the load near the back of the trailer.
Keep the load on one side of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly around turns.
questions.explanation: To prevent rollovers, load cargo as low as possible. Also, take curves and turns slowly.

questions.question: When entering or crossing traffic in a combination vehicle, what is most important?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
Expect other drivers to make room for you.
Wait for other drivers to wave you in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more road space than other vehicles. You must have a large enough gap in traffic to enter or cross safely.

questions.question: Driving a combination vehicle usually requires ____ skill than driving a single vehicle.

options.text: Less
About the same
More

questions.correctAnswerText: More
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are heavier and longer than single commercial vehicles. They require better driving skills.

questions.question: Which statement about combination vehicles is true?

options.text: They are usually shorter than single commercial vehicles.
They are usually lighter than single commercial vehicles.
They require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
They are easier to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are heavier and longer than single commercial vehicles. This means they need more driving skill.

questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve?

options.text: To speed up in rural areas.
Only to test the trailer brakes.
Together with the brake pedal.
On slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only for testing. Using it while moving can cause a skid.

questions.question: How should you use the trailer hand valve?

options.text: For parking.
Only to test the trailer brakes.
Together with the brake pedal.
On slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve controls the trailer brakes but should only be used for testing. Using it while driving can cause a skid. Do not use it for parking because it can release air pressure and cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?

options.text: When drivers turn too quickly.
When drivers do not drive fast enough.
When drivers pay attention to the road.
When drivers drive illegally.

questions.correctAnswerText: When drivers turn too quickly.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers take turns at high speeds. Take all turns and curves slowly and safely.

questions.question: If your trailer drifts off course while backing, what should you do?

options.text: Keep backing without stopping.
Turn the steering wheel toward the drift.
Turn the steering wheel away from the drift.
Return the steering wheel straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel toward the drift.
questions.explanation: If your trailer drifts while backing, correct it immediately by turning the steering wheel toward the drift.

questions.question: When coupling vehicles, what is important?

options.text: You can assume all vehicles are the same.
Make sure you couple correctly.
Cracks in the mounting are acceptable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure you couple correctly.
questions.explanation: Incorrect coupling of combination vehicles can be very dangerous.
